test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Pipe A usually fills a tank in 6 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom of the tank, it takes extra 2 hours to fill the tank. If the tank is full, then how much time will it take to get emptied due to the leak?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours and due to a leak it takes y hours to fill, the leak alone can empty the tank in (x × y) ÷ (y − x) hours.

Here, x = 6 hours and y = 6 + 2 = 8 hours.

Required time = (6 × 8) ÷ (8 − 6) = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 6 hours

Time taken by Pipe A and Leak together = 6 + 2 = 8 hours

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work (Units)**
 **Efficiency (Units/hr)**
 
 

 Pipe A
 6
 24
 24 ÷ 6 = 4
 
 

 Pipe A + Leak
 8
 24 ÷ 8 = 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of the leak = Efficiency of (Pipe A + Leak) − Efficiency of Pipe A

⇒ Efficiency of the leak = 3 − 4 = −1 unit/hr

⇒ The negative sign indicates that the leak empties the tank at the rate of 1 unit/hr.

⇒ Time taken by the leak to empty the full tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of leak

⇒ Time = 24 ÷ 1 = 24 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 24 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, its efficiency is considered positive (+1/x). If a pipe (or leak) empties it in y hours, its efficiency is considered negative (−1/y).

Combined Work with an Emptying Pipe

When an inlet pipe and an outlet pipe operate together, the net part of the tank filled in 1 hour is given by (1/x) − (1/y).

Emptying a Full Tank

If the filling capacity is less than the emptying capacity, the tank will eventually empty. Time taken to empty = Total capacity ÷ Net emptying rate.
